implementation_scope: classical executable projections of P1/P2/P3, with real TrustedStateStore for same-AES-key restart. Production PQC engine separately validated.

baseline_definition.VULNERABLE: no gate, mutable config, weak fallback, local counter, no metadata AAD
baseline_definition.ALLOWLIST: AES/GCM 128 or 256 and captured trusted Provider checked at entry; no snapshot, request floor, durable nonce or metadata AAD
baseline_definition.PROPOSED: entry gate plus snapshot, fixed Provider object, no failure fallback, key-fingerprinted durable nonce, canonical AAD including tenant/document/key version

scenarios.02: valid SHA-256 plus fixture Provider observes synthetic bytes
scenarios.03: AES-256 requested but AES-128 fallback after preferred failure
scenarios.04: same AES key service restart; same nonce permits plaintext XOR recovery
scenarios.05: v1 metadata bound; AES-128->AES-256/key version transition drops metadata binding in baselines
scenarios.06: mutable config changed to ECB and different version between check and execute

limits: A trusted Provider/JVM/code model. Not malicious privileged Provider isolation. Trial Provider never registered globally; no network or real user data.
statistics: One independent fixture per scenario; repeated runs only diagnose consistency. No blocking-rate estimate.
outcomes: Record even successful attacks on PROPOSED; never impose expected security outcomes.
pqc_extension: Actual BC ML-KEM/X25519 control; real BC registry absence and SunEC-pinned ML-KEM service absence. Entry component allowlist with DH rejection negative control, versus final-suite PQC_REQUIRED floor. JDK17 executed; JDK24 unmeasured.
